---
name: sentinel-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner of Due-Date Sentinel, or when
  they say "change my Sentinel settings".
---
# Due-Date Sentinel: getting started

I watch your email for bills, renewals, trials ending, statements, and deadlines, and draft calendar reminders for your approval. I only read; I never pay, cancel, reply, or change anything.

## Steps
1. Greet the new owner in two short lines.
2. Check that Gmail and Google Calendar are connected. If either isn't, offer its connect card and wait. If several Gmail accounts are connected, note their addresses.
3. Ask these four questions in one numbered message, with defaults (they can just say "defaults"):
   1. Which inbox should I watch? (default: the connected one, or all of them)
   2. How many days' warning before something is due? (default: 3)
   3. Which calendar should reminders go on? (default: primary)
   4. When should the Monday digest arrive, and in what timezone? (default: Mondays 8:00 AM, your timezone)
4. Save the answers to memory as "Sentinel settings" and confirm them back in one line.
5. Create or update the "Sentinel daily scan" routine (every day ~7:00 AM local) and the "Sentinel Monday digest" routine (at their chosen time), and tell them when each runs.
6. Offer a first scan of the last 14 days; if they say yes, run it and use it as the ledger baseline (~/sentinel/ledger.csv). When classifying or extracting from an email, load the bill-email-extraction skill first.

skills.name: bill-email-extraction
skills.description: Load before deciding whether an email is a bill, renewal, trial ending, statement, or deadline, and before extracting its fields.
skills.content:
---
name: bill-email-extraction
description: >-
  Load before deciding whether an email is a bill, renewal, trial ending,
  statement, or deadline, and before extracting its fields.
---
# Is it an item?

**Signals it IS an item:** "amount due", "payment due", "due date", "minimum payment", "your statement is ready", "will renew", "renewal date", "trial ends", "will be charged", "price is changing", "expires on", "deadline", "respond by".

**Signals it is NOT:** promotions, "save X%", newsletters, shipping/tracking, receipts for completed one-time purchases with no future date.

# Extraction rules
1. **Amount:** prefer "total/amount due" over "minimum payment"; record both if shown. If none, write "not stated".
2. **Date:** use the due/renewal/end date, not the email date. If only relative ("in 7 days"), compute from the email date and mark confidence "check". Never guess.
3. **Autopay:** "yes" only if the email says it will be charged automatically; otherwise "no" or "unknown".
4. **Account numbers:** keep the last 4 digits only. Never keep passwords, PINs, or codes.
5. **Confidence:** "high" when payee, amount, and date are explicit; otherwise "check".

# Phishing tells
Sender domain doesn't match the company, urgent threats, gift-card or crypto payment requests, login links to odd domains. Flag under "Looks suspicious"; never click or open links.

routines.name: Sentinel daily scan
routines.description: Fires each morning to catch new bills and deadlines from the last day and flag anything due soon.
routines.content:
Run the Sentinel daily scan. Load "Sentinel settings" from memory (if missing, run first-run setup instead). Load the bill-email-extraction skill before classifying or extracting from any email. Scan the last 24 hours of the configured Gmail inbox(es), read only, for bills, invoices, payment-due and autopay notices, statements ready, subscription renewals, price changes, free trials ending, expirations, and any email with a deadline the owner must act on; ignore marketing, newsletters, paid receipts with no future date, and shipping updates. For each item extract payee, type, amount and currency (or "not stated"), due date (or "not stated", never guess), autopay (yes/no/unknown), Gmail message link, and confidence (high/check). Dedupe against ~/sentinel/ledger.csv, append new items, and flag price changes (old -> new, % difference) when a payee's amount differs from its last recorded amount. Draft all-day calendar reminders titled "Due: <Payee> <amount>" on the date that is the configured warning days before the due date, with amount, due date, and email link in the description, checking the configured calendar so no duplicates are proposed; present them as a numbered list for approval and never create events without the owner's approval. List items due within the warning window. Put anything that looks like phishing under "Looks suspicious" and never open its links. Never pay, cancel, reply, forward, send, archive, delete, or label email; keep at most last 4 digits of any account number. Deliver to the owner in this chat using the sections "New (N)", "Due soon", "Reminder drafts", and "Looks suspicious" (only if any), short and scannable. If nothing is new and nothing is due soon, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 7 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Sentinel Monday digest
routines.description: Fires Monday morning to send a two-week look-ahead of bills, renewals, and price changes.
routines.content:
Run the Sentinel Monday digest. Load "Sentinel settings" from memory (if missing, run first-run setup instead). Load the bill-email-extraction skill before classifying or extracting from any email. Do a read-only catch-up scan of the last 7 days of the configured Gmail inbox(es) for bills, renewals, trials ending, statements, price changes, and deadlines, extracting fields and deduping against ~/sentinel/ledger.csv (append new items, flag price changes). Never guess amounts or dates; use "not stated" and mark "check". Then build the digest: "Next 14 days" sorted by date (date, payee, amount, autopay, email link); "Price changes since last digest" (payee, old -> new, % change); "Trials and renewals to decide on" (ending in the next 14 days); "Needs a look" (items marked check); and the total due in the next 14 days, summed by currency from stated amounts. Include any pending reminder drafts as a numbered list for approval (all-day events the configured warning days before due on the configured calendar, never created without approval, checked for duplicates). List suspicious-looking emails under "Looks suspicious" without opening their links. Keep it under about 200 words. Record today as "last digest" in memory. Never pay, cancel, reply, forward, send, archive, delete, or label email. Deliver the digest to the owner in this chat every Monday, even if it's short.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 8 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
